evidence: A published vulnerability-disclosure channel — SECURITY.md or .well-known/security.txt — exists in the checkout, non-empty and content-anchored, so a change to the promise kills the evidence
expected_output: One observation row with disclosure_present, path, bytes and non_empty

assertions.description: A disclosure channel is published at one of the paths a reporter looks: SECURITY.md (root, .github/, docs/) or security.txt (.well-known/, root).
The published file has content. A zero-byte SECURITY.md is a path that resolves and a channel that says nothing.

caveats: The front door, not the programme. Nothing here shows a report arrived, that anyone answered it, or that the address the document names is monitored — and the file is read in place rather than fetched from the published URL, so a channel that is committed but not served still passes. RA-05 (11)'s adjudication carries the remainder in full.
notes: Empty-set discipline — Witness: repo-facts always emits exactly one row carrying disclosure_present, so a repository that publishes no channel violates honestly rather than passing over zero rows; an empty observation set here could only mean the collector never ran. `non_empty` is a byte count and nothing more — a file of blank lines passes it, and whether the text names a contact, a scope or a response timeline is the adequacy limb this recipe does not claim.

plain.checks: Looks for a security policy file — SECURITY.md at the repository root, in .github/ or in docs/, or a security.txt under .well-known/ — and records what it hashes to.
plain.violation: There is no published way to report a vulnerability in this code. Someone who finds one has to guess: a public issue that tells everybody at once, an email address nobody monitors, or silence until the flaw is used.
plain.fix: Add a SECURITY.md naming where reports go, what is in scope, and how fast you answer — then make sure the address it names reaches a person. The file is the half a repository can show; someone reading what arrives is the half it cannot.
